tripRule: Trips are as reported in the covering email, which supersedes the workbook derivation.
movementRule: One movement is one transfer between locations: port to rig, rig to port, or rig to rig. Repositioning at the rig already occupied does not count, nor does a shift between two port-side locations.

trucks.rule: Count truck and pickup units per movement. A dispatch counts as out, an arrival counts as in. An offload of a unit already counted on arrival is not a second movement, and a duplicated row sharing a delivery ticket is counted once.

dataNotes: Vessel trips: the email and the Vessel sheet disagree. The email reports CA1 3, CA3 0, CA5 4, Charlie-3 8 (15). Applying the trip rule to the Vessel sheet gives CA1 1, CA3 0, CA5 1, Charlie-3 6 (8). The email's figures are used, per the standing rule. The same gap appeared in report 24 (13 against 8).

OD1's target well changed between reports. Report 25 had OD1 awaiting BOUM-0001 clearance; this email says SH-0001, in both the current operation and next steps. Port E34 on 21.09 still carries a BM1 call-off (OD-BM1-E-4-3). Confirm the target.

RM-SP-9003 is used twice on 17.09. Port E6 (Odfjell TRS tools to Odfjell) and E7 (COSL backloads from OD1 and OPH to COSL) carry the same delivery number with different cargo and destinations. Counted as two trucks.
Port E8 delivery number reads RM-SP-900. It is truncated. The numbers around it run 9001, 9002, 9003 and then 9005 on 19.09.
